latestChanges: HTML is a Living Standard (continuous updates), not a versioned "HTML6" release model.
Modern declarative attributes like `popover` and `inert` reduce JavaScript needed for common UI behavior.
Performance-oriented attributes such as `loading="lazy"` are widely used for faster mobile pages.
Form and accessibility mappings are continually refined for better assistive-tech and cross-browser consistency.
html.problemItSolves: HTML provides the universal structure and meaning of web content, making pages readable by browsers, search engines, and assistive technologies while enabling responsive mobile layouts.
historyNotes: 1991: Tim Berners-Lee published the first HTML tag set for linked documents.
1995: HTML 2.0 became the first formal standard.
1997: HTML 4.x emphasized separation of structure from presentation (with CSS).
2014: HTML5 became a major milestone with semantic elements and rich media support.
Now: WHATWG maintains HTML as a Living Standard with ongoing incremental improvements.

practiceChallenges.title: 5-Minute Semantic Upgrade
practiceChallenges.prompt: Replace a `div`-only page with `header`, `main`, `section`, and `footer`. Keep it to one phone screen.

practiceChallenges.title: Accessible Image Card
practiceChallenges.prompt: Build a card with an image, heading, short text, and link. Use meaningful `alt` text and logical heading order.

practiceChallenges.title: Mobile Form Essentials
practiceChallenges.prompt: Create a sign-up form using `label` + matching `id`, proper input types (`email`, `tel`), and `required` fields.

practiceChallenges.title: Daily Reflection Snippet
practiceChallenges.prompt: Write a short journal entry using semantic text tags (`article`, `time`, `p`) and validate the HTML.

practiceChallenges.title: Mini Landing Page Skeleton
practiceChallenges.prompt: Create a fast-loading page skeleton with viewport meta, semantic landmarks, and lazy-loaded image placeholders.

antiCheatRules: Show one question at a time on mobile; lock submitted answers to prevent answer fishing.
Shuffle answer options and blank options on each attempt.
Require a one-sentence rationale after each multiple-choice answer.
Use equivalent but randomized code templates (text/content swaps) per learner.
Score code challenges only when all blanks are correct and markup remains valid.
Limit immediate retakes (cooldown) and require reviewing explanations before retry.

multipleChoice.question: Which organization maintains the HTML Living Standard today?
multipleChoice.explanation: HTML is maintained continuously by WHATWG.

multipleChoice.question: Which statement is most accurate about modern HTML evolution?
options: HTML is frozen and no longer changes.
HTML6 replaced HTML5 as a single new standard.
HTML evolves continuously as a Living Standard.
Browsers must wait for infrequent major HTML releases.
multipleChoice.explanation: HTML now updates incrementally instead of by rare large version jumps.

multipleChoice.question: What is the main purpose of `<!doctype html>`?
multipleChoice.explanation: The doctype tells browsers to render in standards mode.

multipleChoice.question: Why prefer semantic elements like `main` and `nav` over generic `div`s?
options: They improve meaning for accessibility and tooling.
They are required for JavaScript to run.
They replace the need for CSS classes.
multipleChoice.explanation: Semantic tags communicate structure to assistive tech, search engines, and developers.

multipleChoice.question: Which tag improves mobile layout scaling behavior?
multipleChoice.explanation: Viewport meta controls how the page scales and fits device width.

multipleChoice.question: For accessibility, what should `alt` text on informative images do?
options: Describe the image’s meaning in context
multipleChoice.explanation: Useful `alt` text communicates the image’s purpose, not raw file details.
